body.heading: The 3 p.m. mystery
paragraphs: Irritable, foggy, unable to concentrate, convinced everything is going wrong — and then you remember you skipped lunch and have had nothing to drink since morning. The body whispers before it shouts, and its whispers are easy to misread as mood or character.

A useful habit: when you feel strangely off, run the basics first. Have I eaten recently? Had water? Moved in the last few hours? Slept last night? Fix whichever is missing before drawing bigger conclusions.

body.heading: Make basics automatic
paragraphs: Basics stay done when they need no decisions: a water bottle that travels with you, a snack in the bag, a walk built into the journey home. Routine beats resolve, especially on busy days.

None of this replaces proper care — ongoing low mood, exhaustion or appetite changes deserve a real conversation with a health professional. But for the ordinary mid-afternoon slump, the boring basics are a surprisingly good first answer.

takeaway: Feeling off? Check food, water, movement and sleep before anything else.
